newsitem.title: UK: Dated Brent firm on US demand, other grades stable.
newsitem.headline: Dated Brent firm on US demand, other grades stable.

text.p: North Sea crudes firmed on Wednesday, pushed higher by buyers looking for Brent to take to the U.S. Gulf but some grades were beginning to run into resistance, traders said.

Dated Brent cargoes sold twice at June Brent -27 cents on Wednesday, the first to a U.S. refiner filling a VLCC loading around May 10 and the second to a trader who paid June Brent less 29 cents for a cargo on Tuesday.
Traders said talk of others offering Brent cargoes into the U.S. Gulf late on Tuesday was adding to the positive tone on North Sea markets.
Brent paper markets were mixed, June Brent slipping two cents to $18.59 a barrel by 1218 GMT, but intermonth spreads were narrowly firmer, dealers said.
June/July talked at -9/-7 cents after trading at -10/-11 cents in late U.S. dealing and July/August showed a similar gain firming to -8/-6 cents after a deal at -10 cents on Tuesday.
Brent CFDs were broadly steady in thin activity, the May 5-9/May 12-16 roll trading at flat.
Other North Sea grades looked to have hit a peak for the time being, May 19-21 Forties fetching Dated Brent +20 cents after trade on Tuesday at +22 cents.
In the Mediterranean, Urals held steady with two deals reported from Tuesday.
A May 8-9 cargo was sold to a refiner at Dated Brent -97.5 cts c+f (-96 cts cif equiv) and a May 16-17 cargo was picked up by a trader/refiner at a $1.00 discount to Dated Brent.
A prompt (May 1-2) 80,000-tonne Urals cargo was offered on the market but the seller was heard asking refiners for a swap for a large ship.
Delays of 2-4 days were still occuring on Novorossissk loadings following recent closures due to bad weather, one lifter said.
The single offer of May Kirkuk seen on the spot market on Tuesday has been withdrawn and the cargo was now heard destined for the owner's own refinery.
"There may be one for sale at the end of the month but I think it's just an optimisation and already has a home. It looks like it's all gone," one lifter said.
